Package org.apache.juneau.rest.server

Class RestContextProperties

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.rest.server.RestContextProperties
@ConfigProperties(prefix="RestContext") public class RestContextProperties extends Object
The env-driven RestContext.* default properties for a resource, resolved as a single bound object.

Each property supplies the environment-level default for the corresponding @Rest attribute (for example getClientVersionHeader() backs @Rest(clientVersionHeader)). A resource's @Rest annotation values, when present, take precedence over these defaults; these properties only establish the starting value before the annotation chain is applied.

Values are resolved under the RestContext prefix from the standard Settings source chain (thread-local override, global override, registered property sources, system properties, system environment) as well as any per-resource PropertySource beans registered in the resource's bean store — so a resource's @Rest(config=...) file can set a RestContext.* key and have it take effect. Relaxed key matching is enabled, so a key may be spelled in camelCase, dotted, or SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE form.

A key absent from every source leaves the corresponding property at its default value shown below. The bound instance for a resource is retrievable via RestContext.getRestContextProperties() or from the resource bean store via beanStore().getBean(RestContextProperties.class).

The RestContext.uriAuthority and RestContext.uriContext settings are intentionally not part of this bean: they carry a null-versus-empty distinction that is represented separately on RestContext. The juneau.restLogger.level setting is likewise separate, as it is owned by the call-logger subsystem rather than RestContext.

    • getDisableContentParamRaw

      public String getDisableContentParamRaw()
      The raw (unresolved) @Rest(disableContentParam) default — whether the &content= URL parameter is disabled.

      The value is stored verbatim — without SVL variable resolution or boolean conversion — because SVL resolution requires the resource's var resolver, which this bean does not carry. RestContext reads this raw value, resolves any SVL variables, and parses it to a boolean.

      Returns:
      The raw value. Never null.
